**Fieldbook 2.0.1 beta 4** (a beta)
The fourth beta, on the beta channel: a Mac with an earlier beta gets it as an automatic update (**Fieldbook › Check for Updates…** to get it at once). Everyone else stays on 2.0 until 2.0.1 itself.
### Added - **The email Inbox:** emails from your email folder (such as a Gmail label) wait in an **Inbox** instead of popping up, even during a call. The **Inbox** button at the top of the window says how many (so do the Dock icon and the menu-bar menu); click it (or **File › Email Inbox…**, Shift-Command-E) to file each one as a new meeting or in a folder's **Emails**, where its people's domains suggest, in the background while you keep working. Several labeled at once each go their own way, and they wait through a restart until you file or dismiss them. A downloaded email still asks right away, except while you're recording, when it waits in the Inbox too.
### Changed - **The toolbar stays put:** **Notes | Transcript**, **Inbox**, and **Update All** are always in the same places, greyed out when they don't apply, so moving through the meeting list no longer shifts the buttons around. - **Text size covers the meeting list and Help:** the A A buttons and Command-Plus/Minus now also size the meeting list (its rows grow with the text) and **Fieldbook Help**, which has the same buttons in its toolbar. - **Help covers Apple Mail:** **Getting Emails into Fieldbook** now explains bringing emails in from Apple Mail: a Gmail account's labels show up as mailboxes there (move an email to **Fieldbook**), an Exchange account's flags sync for the Microsoft 365 flow, and any account can drag emails in.
### Fixed - **Update All waits while the Mac is locked:** the AI key can't be read while your Mac is locked, so a run that hit a lock failed every step after it. Now it pauses until you unlock, tries again a step the lock interrupted, and **Try All Again** retries everything that failed. - **No hitches while recording:** Update All's check for what's out of date no longer runs while you're recording (it waits until you stop), so taking notes in a call stays smooth.

**Fieldbook 2.0.1 beta 3** (a beta)
The third beta, on the beta channel: a Mac with beta 2 gets it as an automatic update (**Fieldbook › Check for Updates…** to get it at once). Everyone else stays on 2.0 until 2.0.1 itself.
### Added - **Change a meeting's date and time:** click the date under its title, or right-click it in the list › **Change Date and Time…**. Its length stays, and its folder takes the new date. - **Update All:** a button at the top of the window says how many AI notes, Discovery answers, MEDDPICC, and summaries have something new. Click it to choose which to bring up to date (rewrites start unticked), then they're done one at a time, sending only what's new where they can. Close it and it keeps going; anything that fails says why, with **Try Again**. Also **File › Update All…** (Shift-Command-U), and **Update <customer>…** on a customer's Account for that customer alone. - **Getting Emails into Fieldbook** in Help: every way to bring emails in, from downloading or dragging one to watching **Downloads** or a Google Drive or OneDrive folder, with step-by-step setup for a Gmail label (the Fieldbook Inbox script, in a box that opens to show what it creates and does, with **Copy**) and for flagging emails in Outlook with Microsoft 365 (a Power Automate flow). - **Fold an email:** in a customer's **Emails**, click the open email's subject (or its row in the list again) to fold it to one line with the sender and date, so the list and the Emails summary stay close together. It stays folded until you open an email.
### Changed - **The account summary reads the account's emails and its meetings' attachments,** not only meetings and notes, and when one is added it offers **Update**, which reads and sends just the new ones. Including the customer's other files stays your choice (**Without the Files**). A summary written before shows its emails and attachments as new the first time.
### Fixed - **Imported Zoom files are dated when the meeting was:** Zoom's cloud recording names (`GMT20261008-150159_…`) give the meeting's start (in UTC, shown in your time), and a name with a date and time (such as Zoom's local `2026-10-08 10.01.59` folders) gives both, instead of when the file was imported. They're named **Zoom chat**, **Zoom transcript**, or **Zoom captions** instead of the file name. - **Long AI replies no longer fail:** a meeting's notes whose reply runs past the AI's length limit are written again from smaller parts of the meeting, and an update to notes, MEDDPICC, or a summary that runs too long is written in full instead. - **A customer's Discovery reads every document even when one fails,** and says which one didn't work. - **Discovery no longer fails on a long, detailed document:** when a file answers so many questions that the AI's reply runs past its length limit (a long slide deck about a customer did), Fieldbook asks about the questions in smaller sets instead of stopping the update. Meeting Discovery does the same.

**Fieldbook 2.0.1 beta 2** (a beta)
The second beta, and the first on the beta channel: install it by hand once, and later betas come as updates (Settings › General › Updates › Get beta versions). Everyone else stays on 2.0 until 2.0.1 itself (build 25 or later).
### Added - **A beta channel:** a Mac that installs a Fieldbook beta gets each new beta as an automatic update, as well as every full release; everyone else only ever gets full releases. In a beta, **Settings › General › Updates › Get beta versions** turns it off (you stay on your version until the next full release) or back on. A beta shows which it is, such as "Version 2.0.1 beta 2". - **Ask AI in Help:** in **Help › Fieldbook Help**, type a question in the search field and press Return, or click **Ask AI about Fieldbook** above the topics it finds. The AI answers from the manual, with links to the sections it used, and takes follow-ups. Only the question and those sections are sent to your AI. - **Microsoft Security is back** in **Settings › AI › Company and Solutions**, with its solutions list ready to use. Zscaler stays the default. - **Emails for each folder:** customers, Internal, Training, Partners, and every label have an **Emails** row under **Files**. It lists the folder's emails newest first (date, sender, subject, attachments); click one to read it, open its attachments, or open it in your email app. **Write** under **Emails summary** summarizes them, linked to the emails behind each point. Add emails by dropping `.eml` files (Gmail's **⋮ › Download message**, or dragged from Mail or Outlook) on **Emails** or the folder in the sidebar, with **Add Emails…**, or by choosing **Add to a customer's Emails** when Fieldbook asks where a downloaded email goes. Emails already added to a folder's Files show here. - **A meeting's AI notes read its attachments:** emails (such as the agenda before or the follow-up after, with their own attachments), PDFs, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and text files, and the words in screenshots and images (on-device text recognition; the picture isn't sent). They're background, linked as **Email** or **Attachment** in the notes' sources and never treated as said in the meeting, and cut short when long so the meeting comes first. Adding, changing, or removing an attachment makes the notes out of date. A meeting made from a file or an email already has its text in **Your notes**, so it isn't read twice. - **An email folder:** **Settings › General › Downloads and Email Folder › Email folder** watches a folder you choose, such as the Google Drive folder the Gmail label script saves to (Fieldbook Inbox). Each email that arrives there, even while Fieldbook was closed, asks where it goes (a new meeting, a customer's Emails, or a meeting), with the customer picked from its people's email domains. - **Settings › Permissions lists the optional permissions** with what each is for: **Calendars** (naming and filing recordings, the next meeting in the menu bar, pre-call briefs), **Reminders** (the bell on to-dos), and the **Downloads folder** (AirDropped iPhone recordings and downloaded emails), with **Allow…** or a way back to System Settings. - **Ask AI searches your folders' emails:** passages of emails that match the question (or come from a customer it names) go with the meetings, and the answer can cite them; click one to show the email. - **A customer's MEDDPICC and recommended stage use its emails** (the customer's and its labels' **Emails**) as evidence beside its meetings and account notes, linked under **Emails**. Adding, changing, or removing an email makes MEDDPICC out of date.
### Changed - **The Welcome window is for anyone:** step 1 is **Bring your own AI**: Apple's on-device model, a local model you run, or a cloud model by API, with where Zscaler employees (their company's AI endpoint) and Microsoft employees (the GitHub Copilot API) get theirs. `zscaler.com` is still filled in as your domain, and Zscaler's AI endpoint as the cloud endpoint.
### Fixed - **Links in Ask AI and Help answers aren't clickable:** an answer's text could include a web link written by the AI (for example, from hidden text in an email); only the citation chips open now. - **The Gmail label script uses only your own folder:** it now saves to the **Fieldbook Inbox** folder you own at the top of My Drive and remembers it, never a folder of the same name someone shared with you. Paste the new script into your Apps Script project and run **setUp** again. - **New Customer, New Label, and Email Domains and Addresses are readable again** in light mode with a dark sidebar (Fieldbook's style and others): their text was light on a light sheet. - **Emails in Files are read for the AI:** an email (`.eml`) kept in a customer's, Internal's, Training's, Partners', or a label's Files, or attached to a customer's meeting, is now read for the files summary, the account summary, and Account Discovery: who it's from and to, when it was sent, its text, and the text of its attachments (PDFs, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, images, text, and forwarded emails). In beta 1 Fieldbook said it couldn't read it. - **Screenshots pasted into an email are kept:** an image in an email's text (such as a screenshot pasted into a Gmail message) comes in with its attachments, so a meeting made from the email has it attached, and summaries read its words. Small images such as signature logos and tracking pixels are still left out. - **Dragging a meeting export from Google Drive into Fieldbook imports it,** instead of saying "Couldn't open the .zip file" (a file Drive hadn't downloaded yet was removed before it was imported).

Offered to 1.8 and later as an automatic update. Everything since 1.9, including what the three betas brought.
### Added
- **Styles:** Settings › General › Look › **Style** offers twelve looks, each in light and dark: **Fieldbook** (the new standard: cream paper, kraft brown, serif headings, ruled lines under your notes), **Fieldbook Legacy** (the 1.x look), Cyber, Blueprint, Solarized, Graphite, Forest, Orchid, Cyberpunk, Matrix, Medieval, and Sci-Fi. **Two-tone** (on by default) puts the sidebar and toolbar in the style's cover color; selected rows take the style's color after **Reopen Fieldbook**; **Font** (also the **Aa** button above your notes) sets the font for notes and transcripts. - **Welcome to Fieldbook 2.0** opens once after updating: pick a look, and see everything new with where to find it. - **Mute Fieldbook:** muting Zoom or Teams doesn't mute your Mac's microphone, so Fieldbook can now be muted itself, with **Control-Option-Command-M**, **Mute** in the Recorder or the toolbar, or the menu-bar icon. Silence is recorded in place of your microphone, a "Fieldbook is muted" panel stays on screen, the call's audio keeps recording, and anything said while muted is left out of the transcript. - **Level meters and microphone warnings** in the Recorder: both tracks' levels while recording, and a warning at once when your microphone clips, is too quiet, or delivers no sound, with what to do. A microphone that delivers nothing is started again after 4 seconds. - **Choose the microphone in the Recorder:** it names the microphone Fieldbook will record; click it to pick another, before or during a recording. - The meeting header names every microphone recorded, in the order used ("Microphone: 33:12 (Rode NT-USB)"), with notes such as AirPods being in headset mode during the call. - **Merge Meetings…** (right-click two or more recordings): a meeting recorded in parts, or started on the iPhone and finished on the Mac, becomes one meeting, transcribed again as a whole, with the joins marked and the originals in the Trash. - **Space** plays and pauses a meeting's audio (not while you type). - **Speakers:** **Add Speaker…** for someone the transcription missed, click a paragraph's name to give it to someone else, **People you've met** suggested from remembered voices, and **Detect Speakers Again…** with how many people spoke on each track. - **Account Discovery:** a **Discovery** row under each customer's Account shows every discovery question with the answer from all of its meetings, account notes, files, and attachments, with sources and dates, earlier or differing answers, filters, and **Copy All**. Pre-call briefs leave out questions already answered. - **Update** instead of a full rewrite for AI notes (**Update Notes**), account summaries, MEDDPICC, and files summaries: when something was only added, only that is sent to your AI endpoint, for far fewer tokens (cloud endpoints). - Discovery questions are numbered as in Salesforce (Q1 to Q253), in each meeting, the brief, **Copy**, and CSV export and import. - **Where each meeting is filed:** its folder and label after the title, in the folders' colors, with **Move To** beside them, and a short path before each title in All Meetings and Archive. - **Arrow keys:** Right goes from the folders to the meetings, then from Notes to Transcript; Left goes back. Right on a folder with hidden labels opens it first, and Left closes it. - Recordings paused on the iPhone (Fieldbook for iPhone) show how long they were paused, and nothing from the paused time is transcribed.
### Changed
- The microphone is recorded through a capture session bound to that one device, so changing headphones or the Mac's output can no longer interrupt it. - With no call, Fieldbook doesn't record a nearby iPhone's microphone on its own unless it's the only one. A microphone you picked is noted as "the microphone you chose". - Set up for Zscaler: a new install goes straight to the Zscaler setup steps, with Zscaler's AI endpoint filled in, `zscaler.com` as your domain, and Company and Solutions preloading Zscaler. Settings already saved don't change. - Discovery costs less: only new questions are matched (**Match Them**, **Update All**), renames don't make it out of date, and with Claude (a Claude API key or a LiteLLM proxy) the question list is read from Claude's prompt cache; Settings › AI › Usage shows how much came from the cache. - MEDDPICC's refresh after a new customer meeting adds only that meeting's evidence, and skips a meeting with nothing to read. - Renaming a speaker or the meeting no longer makes AI notes or Discovery out of date; the new names go into the notes without the AI. - Automatic AI notes are skipped for a meeting with an empty transcript and no notes of yours (**Write Notes** still works). - A meeting always opens on **Notes**; a search result or citation opens the transcript at its line. - The red REC timer in the toolbar is a Stop button. - Help covers everything new, including **Merging Recordings**, **Updating Instead of Rewriting**, **Recordings from your iPhone**, and how to send a meeting with its audio along with a diagnostic report. - Settings › AI's data notice says that meeting attachments' text is sent when you choose **Update** in a customer's Discovery.
### Fixed
- Transcription could hang for good on some completely silent recordings, at every launch. Fieldbook now reads recordings in small pieces, and a meeting cut off twice waits for **Retry Transcription**. - A track that ends before you stop recording is filled with silence to the end. - Importing an export checks each audio track's file name, so a hand-edited export can't point Fieldbook outside the meeting's folder. - On macOS 26, a light frame no longer shows around the sidebar's color. - MEDDPICC no longer fails when a customer has a meeting with nothing to read, such as a silent test recording.
### Since beta 3 (build 21)
- In the sidebar, **Right** on a folder with hidden labels (such as Partners) opens it first; **Right** again moves to the meetings. **Left** closes an open folder. - A microphone you picked yourself, in the Recorder or in Settings, is noted as "the microphone you chose" (it said "chosen in Settings" even when picked in the Recorder). - A meeting's header names every microphone it was recorded from, in the order used, not only the last one; a merged meeting lists all of its parts' microphones. - **Welcome to Fieldbook 2.0** also lists the Recorder's microphone menu, each meeting's folder path, and the arrow keys. - Fixed: MEDDPICC failed when a customer had a meeting with nothing to read, such as a silent test recording moved there; it now skips that meeting, as automatic notes do. - Fixed: following the call app's microphone was logged as a warning ("microphone interrupted") in the activity log; real interruptions still are. - Fixed: on macOS 26, a light frame showed around the sidebar's cover color (macOS 26 floats the sidebar a little in from the window's edges, and the meeting list's color showed around it); the sidebar's own color now fills that space, also in the Help window.

Offered to 1.8 and later as an automatic update. Everything since 1.8.3, including what the two betas brought.
### Added
- **Pre-call briefs:** before a meeting with a customer or partner, click **Prepare Brief** in the menu-bar menu. The brief has the invite's agenda (without links, dial-ins, or passcodes), who's invited and whether they've been in earlier meetings, where things stand, what happened last time, what's still open, goals for the meeting, and, for customers, 5 to 10 Discovery questions this account hasn't answered yet, picked for the agenda. Everything links to the lines behind it. A recorded meeting keeps its brief in its Notes. - **Vocabulary:** names and terms are spelled your way in new transcripts. Words that sound like one are respelled, such as "Netscope" to "Netskope" or "Quabina Mensa" to "Kwabena Mensah". Fieldbook uses the meeting's invitees, its customer and label, saved voices' names, your company's solutions, and your own list in **Settings › Transcription › Vocabulary**. Ordinary words are never changed; point at a paragraph to see what was heard. - **Settings › General › Microphone:** Automatic (the microphone your call app uses, else the Mac's, without opening a Bluetooth headset no app is using) or a microphone you pick.
### Fixed
- Calls no longer sound muddy in AirPods (or another Bluetooth headset) because Fieldbook is recording. Fieldbook now records the microphone your call app uses (Zoom, Teams, or any other app already using a microphone, such as GoTo, RingCentral, or Krisp), follows it when you switch microphones mid-call, and otherwise doesn't open a Bluetooth headset's microphone when another one is connected. AirPods as your microphone and headphones work fine: Fieldbook records the same microphone and doesn't change how the call sounds. Each meeting notes which microphone was recorded. - Switching microphones mid-call no longer loses your microphone for the rest of the recording. If it stops (for example while AirPods switch modes), Fieldbook keeps trying to start it again, and the meeting notes the missing part. - Your voice no longer distorts in Fieldbook's recording when the microphone level is set high (for example by Zoom adjusting it): loud peaks are eased below full scale. - The computer's audio no longer stops for the rest of a recording when a monitor is unplugged. Fieldbook starts it again on a display that's still connected (or when one comes back, the display wakes, or the screen is unlocked), and the missing stretch is kept as silence so times still line up. - A meeting now says clearly when part of a track is missing, such as "System audio missing from 19:23 to 19:41.", in the Recorder while recording and on the meeting afterwards. Any break in the computer's audio counts, even a second. - Fewer made-up lines in transcripts: short filler like "Thank you." or "so" where no one was speaking (a microphone that's open but quiet, such as while you're muted in Zoom or Teams, which mute you in the call, not on your Mac; or a quiet call), and lines that repeat themselves over and over, are left out. They're kept in the meeting's transcript file with the reason. - A meeting where no speech was recognized shows its player, so you can still listen to it, and says what was left out and why.
### Changed
- The speech recognition package (WhisperKit) is updated to 1.1.1, a maintenance release with crash fixes. Transcripts of the test recordings came out the same as before. - Help explains which microphone Fieldbook records and why AirPods sound muddy during calls.
### Since beta 2 (build 17)
- Fieldbook keeps trying to restart a microphone that stops, instead of giving up after a second; it lets go of AirPods' microphone within a second of your call app moving off it; and it follows the microphone of call apps it doesn't know (GoTo, RingCentral) or a noise filter such as Krisp.

A minor update.
### Added
- **Tables in your notes and account notes:** paste a table from Google Docs, Word, Excel, Google Sheets, or a web page and it stays a table (tab-separated text becomes one too), or choose **Format › Insert Table…** or the table button in the formatting bar. Double-click a table (or right-click › **Edit Table…**) to change its cells, add or remove rows and columns, or remove it. Tables are saved as Markdown tables; the AI and search read each row as a line. Copying a table to another app pastes it as tab-separated rows. - Spelling is underlined as you type a meeting's title, in **New Manual Meeting** and when renaming a meeting. Nothing is corrected automatically.
### Changed
- Files in a folder's **Files** and meeting attachments can now be up to 500 MB each (was 50 MB). Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and text files over 100 MB are kept but too large to read for summaries; PDFs and images are read at any size.
